history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Bhujiyo Kotho is a 174-year-old historic five-floor tower on the bank of Lakhota Lake, built 1839-1852 under the Jam Sahebs of Nawanagar for security and communication; it was once considered the tallest building in Saurashtra. Its first floor is pierced with rifle holes, an upper level holds a water tank, and a dancing peacock crowns the peak. It was damaged in the 2001 Gujarat earthquake and restored by the Jamnagar Municipal Corporation with the Archaeological Survey of India at a cost of about Rs 25 crore; Phase-1 was inaugurated by Prime Minister Modi on 20 September 2025 and it reopened to tourists on 19 March 2026. Some travel sites (e.g. MakeMyTrip) mislabel it 'Bhujiyo Kotho Temple'; it is a heritage monument, not a place of worship. The CSV name 'Bhujiyo Kotho Temple' should be corrected to 'Bhujiyo Kotho'.

town_description: Jamnagar is a historic port and industrial city in Saurashtra, founded as Nawanagar by the Jadeja Rajputs in the 16th century. It is known for the Lakhota Lake and Palace, Bala Hanuman Temple, and as one of Gujarat's major trade and refining centres.
